newsitem.title: CANADA: TCPL buys stake in Indonesia power project.
newsitem.headline: TCPL buys stake in Indonesia power project.

text.p: TransCanada PipeLines Ltd said on Wednesday it bought a 10 percent indirect interest in Indonesia's huge Paiton project, which includes building and operating two coal-fired power plants.
The Paiton project, in development for the past five years, is one of the largest power projects in southeast Asia.
It includes two 615 megawatt coal-fired plants costing about US$2.5 billion within the Paiton power generating complex on the northeast coast of Java.
The first plant was slated for completion in November 1998 and the second in May 1999, TransCanada said.
TransCanada said it agreed to buy 10 percent of the 12.5 percent interest in the project held by General Electric Co unit General Electric Capital Corp through its Netherlands limited partnership.
Other partners include P. T. Batu Hitam Perkasa with 15 percent, Mission Energy Co with 40 percent and Mitsui & Co Ltd with 32.5 percent.
TransCanada said all financing was arranged for its purchase, and project debt was non-recourse to the company.

"TransCanada is committed to expanding its international operations through prudent investments," company chief executive George Watson said in a statement. "This project enhances our presence in Indonesia and strengthens our position as an integrated energy company."
In Indonesia, regional use of electricity was constrained by a lack of supply, especially in the Java/Bali area, said TransCanada, which recently opened an office in Jakarta.
It said electricity usage was expected to grow by more than 10 percent a year over the next five years.
